message.content:
The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its metabolic demands. In most mammalian cells, you’ll find anywhere from **hundreds to several thousand mitochondria** per cell. For example:

| Cell type | Typical mitochondrial count |
|-----------|-----------------------------|
| Neurons (high energy demand) | ~5 000–10 000 |
| Hepatocytes (liver cells) | ~2 000–5 000 |
| Muscle cells (skeletal or cardiac) | ~1 000–3 000 |
| Epithelial cells (low energy demand) | ~200–500 |

These numbers are approximate averages; individual cells can vary. If you’re looking at a specific cell type or organism, let me know and I can give a more precise estimate.
